title: Sun Yang, ranked 228th, topples top seed Darko Jorgic at WTT Star Contender Muscat as Odo and Hashimoto win
seo_title: WTT Star Contender Muscat day 4: Sun Yang stuns Jorgic
description: WTT Star Contender Muscat day four: 18-year-old qualifier Sun Yang beat top seed Darko Jorgic, Szőcs ended Wei Jingming's run and Odo and Hashimoto won.
standfirst: The 18-year-old Chinese defender won his fifth match in four days, while Bernadette Szőcs came from two games down to end Wei Jingming's run and Japan reached the women's doubles final.
body: Sun Yang, an 18-year-old Chinese defender ranked 228th in the world, knocked out the top seed Darko Jorgic at WTT Star Contender Muscat on Thursday, winning 3-1 in the last 32 for his fifth win in four days since starting in qualifying. The women's top two seeds came through: Satsuki Odo beat Turkey's Ece Harac 3-1 and Honoka Hashimoto beat India's Sreeja Akula by the same score.

Bernadette Szőcs ended the other teenage run of the week, coming from two games down to beat the 17-year-old qualifier Wei Jingming, while Japan put two pairs into the women's doubles semi-finals and India's Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah reached the men's doubles final.
## Sun Yang topples Jorgic

Jorgic, the world No 14 from Slovenia, was top seed only because Dang Qiu and Anders Lind missed the event, and he had not played a match in Muscat before Thursday. Sun had won three qualifying matches and then beaten India's Ankur Bhattacharjee in five games on Wednesday, as Eleven's [day-one report](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-day-one-wei-jingming-sun-yang-batra-bhattacharjee.html) described.

Sun, who chops on the backhand and attacks with the forehand, took a tight first game 13-11 and the second 11-9. Jorgic pulled one back 11-9, but Sun ran away with the fourth 11-5 to finish it in 37 minutes. It was an upset by any measure: Jorgic is ranked 214 places higher, and the win is the biggest of Sun's senior career in Eleven's records. Sun was a world youth team champion with China in 2024.
He meets South Korea's Park Ganghyeon, the world No 44, in the last 16 on Friday. Park beat his compatriot An Jaehyun, the 14th seed, 3-0.
## Odo and Hashimoto through

Odo, the world No 10 and the women's top seed, dropped the second game against Harac and needed 15-13 in the third before winning 11-4, 8-11, 15-13, 11-6. She meets France's Audrey Zarif, who beat Canada's Mo Zhang, the 15th seed, 3-0 with two deuce games.

Hashimoto, the Japanese defender who won [WTT Contender Istanbul on Sunday](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html), lost the second game to Akula but won 11-9, 8-11, 11-7, 11-5. She meets South Korea's Kim Seongjin, the world No 80, who beat Taiwan's Yeh Yi-Tian, the 16th seed, 3-2 in the last match of the day after Yeh had come back from two games down.

South Korea's Joo Cheonhui, the third seed, dropped 11 points in sweeping Slovakia's Tatiana Kukulkova 11-2, 11-4, 11-5, and Miyu Nagasaki, the fourth seed, beat China's Fan Shuhan 3-1, taking the third game 14-12. China's Qin Yuxuan, the seventh seed, edged Japan's Saki Shibata 11-8 in the fifth.
## Szőcs ends Wei's run

Wei, the 17-year-old who knocked out Manika Batra on Wednesday, led Szőcs 2-0 after winning the second game 16-14. The Romanian fifth seed, 31 and the world No 22, took the third 11-9 and the fourth 11-6, then pulled away 11-4 in the decider after 50 minutes. She plays Japan's Sachi Aoki, 19, who also came from two games down, against France's Jia Nan Yuan, the 11th seed.

Taiwan's Cheng I-Ching, the 10th seed, came from 2-1 down against Spain's Maria Xiao and won the decider 11-3. The longest game of the day went to China's Wang Xiaotong, who beat Romania's Elizabeta Samara, the 14th seed, 3-1, taking the third game 20-18; she meets Joo next.
## Kwon Hyuk and the other seeds who fell

South Korea's Kwon Hyuk, an 18-year-old qualifier ranked 106th, beat Egypt's Omar Assar, the 10th seed and world No 28, 11-4 in the fifth game. Romania's Iulian Chirita, 20 and ranked 83rd, knocked out France's Simon Gauzy, the 13th seed, 3-2 after winning the first game 16-14.

Croatia's Tomislav Pucar, the ninth seed, came from two games down to beat China's Huang Youzheng, taking the fourth 12-10 and the fifth 11-9. China's Yuan Licen, a qualifier, beat Portugal's João Geraldo, the 16th seed, and Joe Seyfried beat Germany's Wim Verdonschot, the 15th seed, 3-0.

Shunsuke Togami, the men's second seed, needed 16 minutes and conceded 15 points to beat India's Manav Thakkar 11-6, 11-4, 11-5. Hiroto Shinozuka came from a game down to beat 17-year-old Ryuusei Kawakami 3-1 in the all-Japanese match, recovering from 7-2 down in the third to win it 13-11. South Korea's Oh Junsung, the fifth seed, lost the first game 11-4 to Ryoichi Yoshiyama and then won the next two 11-2, 11-2 before taking the fourth 12-10. Dimitrij Ovtcharov, 38 and the seventh seed, beat the Czech veteran Lubomir Jancarik 3-1 and meets Kwon next.
## Doubles

Thakkar was back on court within hours of his singles defeat and reached the men's doubles final with Shah. They let a two-game lead slip against Germany's Andre Bertelsmeier and Wim Verdonschot in the quarter-finals before winning the decider 13-11, then beat France's Simon Gauzy and Flavien Coton 3-1 in the semi-finals. They play the top seeds Lim Jonghoon and Oh Junsung, who beat Leo De Nodrest and Lilian Bardet 3-1.

In the women's doubles, Saki Shibata and Sachi Aoki beat China's Feng Yixuan and Fan Shuhan 3-1 and Satsuki Odo and Sakura Yokoi beat Wang Xiaotong and Xu Yi 3-1. Shibata and Aoki then lost their semi-final 3-1 to the top seeds Kim Nayeong and Joo Cheonhui, who had beaten Hashimoto and Nagasaki 11-3 in the fifth game of their quarter-final. Odo and Yokoi will meet Kim and Joo in Friday's final after beating Szőcs and Samara 11-8, 11-6, 11-5 in 17 minutes.

France's Esteban Dorr and Jia Nan Yuan knocked out the mixed doubles top seeds, Alvaro Robles and Maria Xiao, 11-9 in the fifth game, and Australia's Nicholas Lum and Yangzi Liu beat China's Yuan Licen and Wang Xiaotong 12-10 in the decider. Togami and Odo beat Park Ganghyeon and Joo 3-0, and Eduard Ionescu and Szőcs also won in straight games.

## Friday: last 16, quarter-finals and doubles finals

The last 16 start at 6am UK time (10am in Muscat), with Odo against Zarif and Togami against Seyfried among the first matches; Sun plays Park at 6.35am. The mixed doubles semi-finals follow at 8.20am: Dorr and Yuan against Ionescu and Szőcs, and Lum and Liu against Togami and Odo. The singles quarter-finals run from 11am to about 3.05pm UK time, and the doubles finals close the day, the women's at 4pm and the men's at 4.50pm. Times are approximate. Eleven's [event page](/events/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026.html#matches) has live scores and the full draw.
